summary: The team is executing a two-track push: fixing an Outlook account lockout that has disrupted email access while advancing the Knowledge website redesign and prioritizing Asia Star and Intelligent China for search/AI visibility.
summaryDetail: The most urgent issue is the Outlook account lockout caused by stale password credentials; the team must delete and re-login on all devices, update passwords on home computers and phones, and confirm with CKGSB that the backend account is unlocked. On the website front, the Knowledge redesign is moving forward with a decision to keep the current look but adopt editorial-style article layouts and bring BCI/BSI indices to the front; a 30-minute working session is needed to mark specific feedback, and Joker will then make design changes. For global marketing, the team has prioritized Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs for search/AI visibility, with the Intelligent China webpage launching this week to enable optimization and traffic campaigns; Joseph is drafting target areas and building customer profiles from Asia Star participants. Upcoming work includes finalizing the ESG report and Business Sentiment Index press release, kicking off promotion for the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum, and reviewing video promotion plans for the Blue Carrot brand video and Asia Start videos.

decisions.text: Re-login and update passwords on all devices to prevent account lockout
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic across the site
Keep the current Knowledge look and feel rather than a dramatic revamp, using the new design mainly for menu categorization changes
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage
Use the article detail page improvements (prominent authors, audio, varied title font sizes, pullout quotes) as a template for authors
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs; Berkeley as optional third; hold US programs (Stanford, Columbia) for now.
Launch Intelligent China webpage this week to enable optimization and traffic-driving campaigns.
